Summary of the equity opportunity.

Marcus & Millichap Capital Corporation is seeking a limited partner equity investment in Wylder Hotel Tilghman Island. The capital retires the existing debt, funds the renovation in full and acquires the adjacent waterfront parcel. The sponsor is targeting a 2.0x equity multiple over a 36-month hold. The size of the investment depends on the senior and preferred capital placed alongside it, and the structure is open for negotiation.

Wylder Hotel Tilghman Island · LP Equity MMCC · The TRANCHE Group02

A 58-key waterfront resort on 8.10 acres, with an adjacent parcel under contract.

Wylder Hotel Tilghman Island sits on Tilghman Island in Talbot County, Maryland, between the Chesapeake Bay and the Choptank River — an 8.10-acre waterfront parcel with 1,100 feet of water frontage, a marina, pool, restaurant and boat bar. Operated under the Wylder Hotels brand, the property is mid-repositioning, with a Small Luxury Hotels affiliation planned for Year 2. The adjacent parcel at 21441 Dogwood Cove — three acres, a four-bedroom residence and 24 boat slips — is under contract and funded in this capitalization; see page 5.

Acquired by 21551 Tilghman Investors LLC, the entity that owns the hotel, so the parcel comes into the partnership rather than a separate venture. The parcel closes on November 18, 2026, shortly after the recapitalization.

The parcel sits at 21441 Dogwood Cove, Tilghman, Talbot County, Maryland.

What It Adds
Boat slips24
Land±3 acres
Residence4 bedrooms
Keys1 · whole-home suite
Site on completion±11.1 acres
Marina slips on completion47

The residence becomes a whole-home suite, a product the hotel cannot offer today, and is counted as the 58th key. Its 24 slips take the marina from 23 slips today to 47 on completion.

It is underwritten conservatively — a $1,500 nightly rate at 35% occupancy, or $191,625 of annual revenue from stabilization.

Why It Matters

The parcel was part of the hotel until it was separated and sold to a third party during a bankruptcy roughly ten years ago. Acquiring it reassembles the original assemblage and takes the last private parcel between the hotel and its waterfront off the market.

The $1,100,000 purchase is funded from the capitalization at closing, with no acquisition debt against the parcel. The $300,000 renovation is funded from the same proceeds.

The estimated values in this package — $21,400,000 as is, $26,000,000 upon completion and $29,500,000 upon stabilization — are for the hotel and do not include this parcel. Every basis, coverage and return figure is measured against them, so what the acquisition is worth is upside those numbers do not carry.

Capitalize the EBITDA the parcel itself produces — the marina and room revenue — at 7.0% and it is worth roughly $4.3 million against a $1.4 million all-in cost.

Ownership and operating structure.

The property is owned by 21551 Tilghman Investors LLC, led by principal John Flannigan, and operated under the Wylder Hotels brand through affiliate Wylder Eastern Shore Management, LLC — controlling day-to-day operations and the renovation, with a Small Luxury Hotels affiliation planned for Year 2.

Structure and Alignment
01Owner-operated, no third-party manager — Day-to-day operations are run by an affiliate of ownership. There is no third-party management agreement to terminate or subordinate, no comfort letter to negotiate and no split incentive between owner and operator.
02Continuous ownership since 2017 — The sponsor has owned and operated the hotel under the Wylder brand through the pandemic cycle and the current repositioning, investing a further $642,693 of capital between 2021 and 2025.
03Single-asset ownership entity — 21551 Tilghman Investors LLC holds this property and, on closing, the adjacent Dogwood Cove parcel — and no other operating assets — keeping the collateral and its cash flow ring-fenced.
04Two-property brand platform — Revenue management, distribution, design and procurement are shared across Wylder Hotels in Maryland and New York, giving a 58-key asset reach it could not support standing alone.

Operating statements are produced monthly at the property level and are the basis for the historical figures in this package. Financial reporting, revenue management and the renovation are handled in-house.

How It Is Funded and Drawn

The program is funded from the capital raised at closing and held back, not paid out in advance. Draws follow contractor pay applications and vendor invoices, against lien waivers and inspection, so money leaves the account as work is put in place.

No construction starts before the senior loan closes, and every date in the program moves day for day with that closing. A delay in the capitalization does not compress the work; it moves it.

The contingency is 10.0% of $2,575,000 of hard costs and is drawn pro rata with hard cost spending rather than held to the end, so the carried balance always reflects the work still to come.

Guestrooms run in four waves rather than closing the hotel, so rooms keep selling through the program and each wave returns to inventory as the next begins. Monthly figures are indicative and carry a dollar of rounding against the exact budget.

Small Luxury Hotels affiliation and distribution.

Why the Affiliation Matters
Hilton Distribution

SLH member hotels are bookable directly through Hilton.com, the Hilton app and Hilton Honors. The affiliation places the property inside Hilton’s reservation and loyalty system rather than leaving it dependent on direct booking and third-party channels, which is the mechanism behind the projected occupancy and rate gain.

An Established Relationship

The sponsor already operates within SLH. Wylder Windham, the sister hotel in the Catskills, is an SLH member and was the first in that market. The application here is an extension of a working relationship rather than a first approach.

American Express Fine Hotels & Resorts

Wylder Windham carries the American Express Fine Hotels & Resorts designation, reached through the SLH platform. The same designation is the plan at Tilghman Island, adding a high-rate corporate and affluent leisure channel on completion.

Affiliation is targeted on completion of the renovation and remains subject to application, inspection, board approval and an executed brand affiliate agreement.

What the Market Trend Supports

Market supply has been unchanged at approximately 404 rooms since 2022, while demand has grown in each of the last two years and reached a ten-year high of 84,017 room nights in 2025. Trailing twelve-month demand through March 2026 is running 5.6% ahead of the prior period. Market RevPAR has compounded at 6.0% a year since 2019 and stands at a record $199. $500,000 of working capital, plus whatever interest and carry reserve the financing requires, so the renovation does not depend on operating cash flow.

The Position

The as-is estimate of $368,966 per key sits below the average of both comparable sets — the East Coast waterfront sales and the eight resort trades closed since January 2025 — and between the median and the average of the more recent set.

The stabilized estimate of $508,621 per key sits below the two highest recent resort trades, at $741,000 and $893,000 per key, and is reached only after a $3,303,000 capital program, the adjacent-parcel acquisition and brand affiliation.

The total cost basis of $331,860 per key remains below the as-is estimate, and the capitalization attaches at $300,070 per key. Every value above is for the hotel alone; the adjacent parcel adds roughly $4.3 million of value against a $1.4 million cost, none of which is in these figures.

What the Valuation Assumes
Scope assumed

A $3,003,000 renovation complete by April 2027; keys from 50 to 57, with four off‑line rooms returned and three added; the second building built out as a spa and wellness center; the marina expanded from 23 to 48 slips; meeting space from 3,722 to 5,252 square feet.

Brand

Small Luxury Hotels of the World membership, and the Hilton booking access that comes with it, assumed upon completion of the renovation.

Operating assumptions

A 3.00% management fee, a 4.00% FF&E reserve, a ten‑year hold, 3.00% growth, a 3.00% cost of sale and an exposure and marketing period of six to twelve months.

Adjustments between scenarios

A $3,500,000 stabilization discount from As Stabilized back to As Complete, and a $4,600,000 total renovation cost adjustment from As Complete back to As Is. $3,000,000 of capital expenditure is deducted in the As Is discounted cash flow.

Prepared for mortgage financing, with reliance limited to the named intended user. An investor relying on it needs its own reliance letter. The Tilghman Island Inn is the nearest transaction and is reported under contract at $5,200,000. It is a 20-key upper-midscale property configured as condominium units on five acres, with 1,800 SF of meeting space and seven slips. It carries neither the key count, the two food and beverage outlets, the marina, the 3,722 SF of event space nor the income base of the subject, and it establishes small-inn pricing on the island rather than resort pricing.

What the Local Set Does Establish

The Tidewater Inn, an 89-key full-service hotel in Easton, is expected to be brought to market in 2026 and reported 2025 occupancy of 48% at a $238 average rate on approximately $950,000 of net operating income. It is the only property in the local set operating at institutional scale, and it does so at a rate 43% below the subject’s $415 stabilized projection and without waterfront, marina or resort positioning. The Robert Morris Inn in Oxford, 16 keys, traded at $200,000 per key in 2024 and is now closed and back on the market at a lower asking price. The local evidence brackets the subject rather than pricing it: small and partly distressed inns below, and a single larger property in a materially different product tier.

The eight resort transactions at left average 44 keys, closely matching the subject at 58, and support a per-key range of $266,000 to $893,000 with a median of $332,000. The estimated as-is value of $368,966 per key sits between that median and the average.
